clue.text: Trade union's enemy in vehicle following Sierra

indicators.note: following says the vehicle comes after Sierra in the answer

parts.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a cab is a vehicle for hire, a taxi

explanation.surface: A union's foe is spotted sitting in a car behind a Ford Sierra.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike-breaker who keeps working during a dispute is the classic enemy of organised labour.

clue.text: Execute second lag

parts.note: to hang someone is to execute them
to second a motion is to back or support it

explanation.surface: A grim instruction: put to death the second convict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lag' looks like a noun for a convict, the partner of 'Execute', but it is the verb meaning to trail behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To lag is to fall behind or hesitate, the same as staying in the rear.

clue.text: Society cheers, receiving Trojan's prize in place of emperor?

indicators.note: receiving says the word for cheers takes the prize inside itself

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers
Helen of Troy was the prize carried off to Troy by Paris

explanation.surface: A club toasts a Trojan's trophy, standing in for an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon was exiled to the South Atlantic island and died there; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The island was Napoleon's final place of exile, so it is a place famously linked to an emperor.

clue.text: Lower layer taken in by Le Pen supporters

definitions.note: to lower (lour) is to scowl, used as a verb

indicators.note: taken in by says the layer sits inside the letters for the supporters

parts.note: FN is the Front National, the French party led by the Le Pen family
a row is a tier or layer, as of seats or bricks

explanation.surface: A lower social stratum is won over by the French far right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' rhymes with 'flower' here: to lour, to look sullen.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour is to look sullen and scowl, which is what a displeased face does.

clue.text: Person striving to comprehend compilers in The Observer

indicators.note: to comprehend is used in its sense of to include or contain, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a vier is one who vies, someone striving to win
crossword setters refer to themselves as we

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to understand the setters in a Sunday newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, which steers the reader away from the plain onlooker sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who watches, like a television watcher, is an observer.

clue.text: Travelling fair around great land mass

indicators.note: travelling suggests the letters of fair moving about into a new order

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around or approximately

explanation.surface: A funfair tours the whole of a vast continent.
explanation.definitionFit: The second-largest continent is one of the world's great land masses.

clue.text: Perhaps boil some spicy stew

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cooking note: you might bring some of the spicy stew to the boil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boil' looks like a cooking verb but is a noun, a skin swelling, and 'Perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A boil is a type of swelling on the skin, loosely grouped with sacs and lumps of that kind.

clue.text: Geordie entertainer plugs singer, one who intones

indicators.note: plugs says the entertainer fills a gap inside the singer

parts.note: Cher is a famous American singer
Ant McPartlin of the TV duo Ant and Dec comes from Newcastle, whose natives are Geordies

explanation.surface: A TV presenter promotes a pop star on his show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugs' suggests advertising, but here it means stops up, sitting inside. Ant and Dec are a famous British TV presenting duo from Newcastle.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who chants, as in a church service, is a person who intones.

clue.text: In short coat from bazaar that is smart

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outside, so take the outer letters of bazaar

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
fly is slang for sharp or smart

explanation.surface: A short coat bought at a market looks rather stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something in short means saying it concisely, in few words.

clue.text: Appear in clothing for bride, extremely loosely fitting

indicators.note: the word for appear goes in, dressed by the outer letters around it
extremely means take the extreme letters, the first and last, of both bride and loosely

parts.note: to seem is to appear

explanation.surface: A dress for the bride looks too loose at the fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fitting' looks like a dressmaker's session but is an adjective meaning proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seemly or becoming is fitting, an old word for appropriate.

clue.text: Cause irritation with the French horn

parts.note: to bug someone is to irritate them
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A French horn played badly is getting on everyone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' looks like one instrument; 'the French' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle is a simple brass instrument of the horn family, used for military calls.

clue.text: Privileged American reporter's useless, middle feature

parts.note: a WASP is a White Anglo-Saxon Protestant, the stereotypical privileged American

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the news, so what follows is a word heard rather than read

parts.note: waste means useless, as in waste ground

explanation.surface: A wealthy American journalist proves useless, a middling performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A very narrow midriff is a figure trait centred on the body's middle.

clue.text: Field creature living on sheep escaped

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word
the ked or sheep ked is a wingless fly that lives on sheep

explanation.surface: Something living in a field feeds off sheep and then got away.
explanation.definitionFit: Information or liquid that has leaked has got out, escaped its container.

clue.text: Bound to have left current US university

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone is sure to have quit their current American college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it is the noun for a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound, as in out of bounds, is a boundary or limit.

clue.text: Criticise person selling fish

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone finds fault with the fishmonger.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to rebuke or find fault with them.

clue.text: Rough recipe to stuff meat dish

indicators.note: to stuff is to fill, so the recipe's letter goes inside the dish

parts.note: hash is a dish of chopped cooked meat
R abbreviates recipe, from Latin for take

explanation.surface: A crude cooking guide to filling a meat dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough treatment is severe or unkind, so rough here means harsh.

clue.text: Dislikes missing the first editions

indicators.note: missing the first says the opening letter of the word for dislikes is dropped

parts.note: aversions are strong dislikes

explanation.surface: Someone hates that the first printings are missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Different versions of a book or text are its editions or variants.

clue.text: Go directly to competition in Korea and inflame rioting

indicators.note: in places the competition inside the jumbled letters
rioting suggests disorder, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a bee is a contest, as in a spelling bee

explanation.surface: A sporting contest in Korea sets off unrest among the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' rearranges two separate words, skipping 'and', into MAKEALINEFOR; 'in' then puts the contest inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees fly straight back to the hive, so the idiom means head straight for somewhere.

clue.text: Struggling alone to preserve Renaissance language

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of alone are in turmoil and rearranged

parts.note: to tin food is to preserve it in a can

explanation.surface: Someone battling alone to keep a Renaissance tongue alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggling' rearranges ALONE as NEOLA, and 'preserve' is the verb tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin revived by Renaissance humanists for scholarship is called the new Latin of that era.

clue.text: Building soon fit to cover grand foundations

indicators.note: to cover means to go round, so the rearranged letters wrap around grand's letter
building means putting together, so the letters of soon fit are assembled in a new order

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A building will soon be ready to pay for its grand foundations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' rearranges SOON FIT, and 'to cover' puts that around G.
explanation.definitionFit: The base courses at the bottom of a wall are its foundations, the ground it stands on.

clue.text: Books about posh rotter in French city

indicators.note: about indicates turning round, so the books are read backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Bible's first part
U means upper-class, posh
a louse is a contemptible person, a rotter

explanation.surface: Literature about an upper-class cad set in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of the Occitanie region in south-west France is a major city.

clue.text: Discontent in leaving EU — insane rubbish!

indicators.note: rubbish is used as a verb meaning to trash, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaving says the word in departs from the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Political discontent: the idea of staying in the EU branded insane rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes IN out of EU INSANE, leaving EUSANE, which 'rubbish' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Unease is anxiety or dissatisfaction, a state of discontent.

clue.text: Nothing to notice, according to timekeeper

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to clock something is British slang for to notice it

explanation.surface: A timekeeper apparently sees nothing to notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from 'of the clock', telling the hour as read from a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying three o'clock means three by the clock, the time a timekeeper shows.

clue.text: US flier's test gets hard, having passed moon

indicators.note: having passed says the test comes after the moon

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons
MOT is the annual UK vehicle roadworthiness test
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An American pilot's exam gets tough after flying past the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: MOT is Britain's yearly car safety test.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American silk moth with eyespots on its wings is a flying insect native to the US.

clue.text: Handy old electrical component

parts.note: a fuse is a safety part of an electric circuit

explanation.surface: An old electrical part still comes in handy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useful or handy is helpful in practice.

clue.text: Project love and females run away

parts.note: to beetle is to overhang or project, as beetling brows do
love is zero in tennis, written O
F abbreviates female, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A romance-and-women plan has fallen through, so off they go.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuttle off quickly like an insect is to hurry away.

clue.text: Lure company of fliers with hanky-panky

parts.note: BA is British Airways, an airline
it is a coy word for sex, as hanky-panky is

explanation.surface: An airline tempts customers with a bit of naughtiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is anything used to entice, a lure or temptation.

clue.text: Addicts overwhelming silly girl

indicators.note: overwhelming says the addicts' letters surround the next piece

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a group of addicts
a nit is a silly person, a nitwit

explanation.surface: A group of addicts gangs up on a foolish young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords often clue women's names by a generic word like girl, and this is one.

clue.text: English composer deserved to get stripped off

indicators.note: stripped off says the word loses its outer covering, its first and last letters

parts.note: having earned something is to have deserved it

explanation.surface: A composer who earned the right to undress.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia! and was an eighteenth-century English musician.

clue.text: They're in all across answers, factionally divided

definitions.meaning: each across answer hides a creepy-crawly: ant, fly, bug, wasp, ked, roach, bee, louse, moth, beetle, nit, midge
split into factions is, read as two words, split into sects

explanation.walkthrough: Every across entry contains a small creature: CHANTER has ANT, SMIDGEN has MIDGE, and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants, flies and beetles are all six-legged bugs, the theme in each across light.

clue.text: Poles consuming small person's tiny portion

indicators.note: consuming says the poles' letters swallow the next piece

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
midge is an informal word for a very small person

explanation.surface: Polish people eat a small person's meagre share.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgen is a very small amount, a tiny bit.
